answer: Practically, the chain should cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because wander only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, canyon is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any tide approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
